answer: Network latency triangulation stops one server from posing as many agents. First, every new agent must answer timed pings from 12 random verifier nodes on five continents. Second, round-trip times reveal where it really sits, since light in fiber can't beat physics. Third, agents whose timing maps to the same rack are merged into one identity. Faking 500 agents in separate regions means renting 500 machines at about $20 a month, so $10,000 a month before earning a single reward. A falcon over a dune can spot every hare that runs to the same river to drink.
